questions.stem: Which of the following is a long-acting β-2 agonist that can be prescribed in a patient with moderately severe bronchial asthma?
questions.solutionHtml:
Formoterol is a long-acting β-2 agonist (LABA).

Beta 2 agonists are classified based on their duration of action into: 

  • Short-acting β-2 agonists (SABA):
    • Salbutamol
    • Terbutaline 
    • Pirbuterol
  • Long-acting β-2 agonists (LABA):
    • Salmeterol
    • Formoterol
  • Very long-acting β-2 agonists (V-LABA):
    • Indacaterol
    • Olodaterol
    • Vilanterol




Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 731 and 732

questions.stem: What is the current GINA recommendation for the prescription of long-acting β-2 agonists in patients suffering from bronchial asthma?

options.label: B
options.text: In combination with an inhaled anticholinergic

options.label: C
options.text: In combination with an inhaled corticosteroid

options.label: D
options.text: In combination with a short acting β-2 agonist

questions.answerText: In combination with an inhaled corticosteroid
questions.solutionHtml:
LABA is used in combination with inhalational corticosteroids (ICS), preferably in the form of a combination inhaler.

LABA is never taken alone as it does not treat the underlying chronic inflammation of asthma. Corticosteroids will decrease the underlying inflammation and halt the progression of the disease.

Short-acting β-2 agonists (SABA) can be given as an add-on therapy to the LABA-ICS combination (as-needed therapy).





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 732

questions.stem: Which among the following is the most appropriate therapy for bronchodilation in acute severe asthma?
questions.solutionHtml:
Nebulized short-acting beta-2 agonists (SABAs) are the most appropriate therapy in acute severe asthma among the given options. 

Nebulized route is preferred over the intravenous route as it is easier and safer with equivalent efficacy.

Intravenous aminophylline is less effective than SABA and is reserved for those who are resistant or intolerant to beta-2 agonists with acute severe asthma. 

Inhalational anticholinergics are not indicated in acute severe asthma as they are less effective than SABAs.





Tintinalli's Emergency Medicine , 8th Ed, page no. 214
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 14th Edition, Page no: 878, 879

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a side effect of salbutamol?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hypoglycemia is not a side effect of salbutamol. It causes hyperglycemia.

The side effects of salbutamol are due to the stimulation of extrapulmonary β2 receptors. They are more common after oral or intravenous administration. The side effects seen are:    

  • Muscle tremor
  • Tachycardia
  • Hypokalemia 
  • Restlessness        
  • Hypoxemia         
  • Increase in free fatty acid, insulin, glucose, pyruvate, and lactate




Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 732
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 14th Edition, Page no: 880

questions.stem: An asthmatic patient complains of wheezing and shortness of breath most days of the week. Which of the following therapies is preferred in him?
questions.solutionHtml:
This patient has persistent asthma for which the preferred therapy is LABA with ICS available as a combination inhaler.

ICS should be started in any patient who needs to use a short-acting beta-2 agonist inhaler for symptomatic control more than twice a week (persistent asthma). 





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 738

questions.stemHtml: A 5-year-old child requires bronchodilator therapy. You attach the device shown below to the pressurized metered-dose inhaler for ease of use. Which of the following is false about this device?

options.label: A
options.text: Decreases the deposition of drug on the oropharynx

options.label: B
options.text: Increases the delivery of drug to lower airways

options.label: C
options.text: Increases the incidence of oropharyngeal candidiasis

options.label: D
options.text: Systemic absorption of drugs is unaffected

questions.answerText: Increases the incidence of oropharyngeal candidiasis
questions.solutionHtml:
The given image is of a spacer device. It decreases the incidence of oropharyngeal candidiasis and other propellant-mediated oropharyngeal adverse effects like dysphonia that occur with the use of a pMDI.

Spacers reduce the velocity and size of particles entering the upper airways. This reduces the amount of drug that impinges on the oropharynx and increases the proportion of drug inhaled into lower airways. The systemic absorption is unchanged by the use of a spacer.

Spacer devices are useful in delivering inhaled drugs to children who are not able to use a pMDI alone but can also be used by adults for better drug delivery. The image below shows the use of a spacer device with a face mask which is preferred in children younger than 3 years of age.



The various devices used for the delivery of inhalational drugs are:

  • Pressurized metered-dose inhalers - Drugs are propelled from a canister in the pMDI with the aid of a propellant. These devices are convenient, portable, and typically deliver 50–200 doses of a drug


  • Dry powder inhalers - these devices scatter the drug into a fine powder that is dispersed by air turbulence on inhalation. DPIs have been developed to deliver drugs such as insulin, but the dosing is inconsistent. Children <7 years find it difficult to use a DPI. 


  • Nebulizers: Two types of nebulizer are available -
    • Jet nebulizers that are driven by a stream of gas (air or oxygen)
    • Ultrasonic nebulizers that use a rapidly vibrating piezoelectric crystal and thus do not require a source of compressed gas.

The nebulizers deliver much higher drug doses as compared pMDIs. These are useful in:

  • Treating acute exacerbations of asthma and COPD
  • Extreme airway obstruction (severe COPD)
  • Delivering inhaled drugs to infants and small children who cannot use the other inhalation devices
  • Administering drugs such as antibiotics in relatively high doses








Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 730

questions.stem: An asthmatic patient has been taking theophylline tablets for symptomatic relief. On which of the following receptors does this drug have an antagonistic action?
questions.solutionHtml:
Theophylline has an antagonistic action on adenosine receptors.

Theophylline is a methylxanthine. It acts as a non-selective PDE inhibitor. Its other actions include: 

  • Increased IL-10 release
  • Decrease in gene transcription of pro-inflammatory cytokines
  • Promotes apoptosis of granulocytes
  • Histone deacetylase activation. The recruitment of histone deacetylase-2 by glucocorticoid receptors switches off inflammatory genes. Through this mechanism, theophylline enhances the anti-inflammatory effects of corticosteroids.

Theophylline can be used as a bronchodilator in an asthmatic patient on ICS as an add-on drug. LABAs are more effective but theophylline is a cheaper option.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 733

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about theophylline is not correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Increase in dose is required in cardiopulmonary disease

options.label: B
options.text: Decreases the breakdown of cAMP in smooth muscles

options.label: C
options.text: Increase in dose is required in smokers

questions.answerText: Increase in dose is required in cardiopulmonary disease
questions.solutionHtml:
A decrease in dose of theophylline is required in cardiopulmonary disease. This is because reduced clearance of theophylline is seen in liver disease, pneumonia, and heart failure.

In smokers, clearance of theophylline is increased due to the induction of CYP1A2 enzyme. 

Theophylline is a non-selective phosphodiesterase inhibitor that decreases the breakdown of cAMP levels in smooth muscles resulting in bronchodilation.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 14th Edition, Page no 883-884, table 44-2

questions.stem: Which of the following is an indication for theophylline?
questions.solutionHtml:
Theophylline is indicated in the treatment of apnea of prematurity.

In apnea of prematurity, methylxanthines such as theophylline and caffeine increase the central respiratory drive by lowering the threshold of response to hypercapnia. They also enhance the contractility of the diaphragm and prevent diaphragmatic fatigue.

Options A & B - The adenosine receptor antagonism property of theophylline precipitates cardiac arrhythmias and epileptic seizures. 

Option C - Theophylline is no longer recommended as a treatment for acute severe asthma by the latest guidelines (GINA 2021) because of its poor efficacy and safety profile. 





Tintinalli's Emergency Medicine , 8th Ed, page no. 598
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, page no. 735
Online Resource, https://ginasthma.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/GINA-Main-Report-2021-V2-WMS.pdf
Nelson textbook of pediatrics 21st edition, Chapter 122.2 Apnea page 931

questions.stem: A patient with severe persistent asthma continues to have symptoms despite being on high-dose ICS-LABA therapy. Which of the following is a leukotriene receptor antagonist, appropriate as an add-on therapy for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Zafirlukast and montelukast are leukotriene receptor antagonists. They are competitive antagonists of the cysLT1 receptors. These drugs act by: 

  • Decreasing bronchoconstriction
  • Reducing airway mucus secretion
  • Decreasing vascular permeability and
  • Reducing eosinophil chemotaxis 

Option A: Dupilumab is an interleukin-4 receptor antagonist used in severe asthma. 

Option B: Roflumilast is a PDE-4 selective inhibitor used in the treatment of COPD.

Option D: Zileuton is a lipoxygenase inhibitor that can be used in the treatment of asthma.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 741

questions.stem: The use of which of the following therapies for acute asthma requires serial monitoring of liver function tests?
questions.solutionHtml:
Zileuton, montelukast, and zafirlukast are all associated with rare instances of hepatic dysfunction.  Liver function tests should be monitored during the course of their therapy.

Therapy with selective β-2 agonists (salbutamol, salmeterol) does not require serial monitoring of LFTs.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 741

questions.stem: An elderly asthmatic on treatment presented with fever, malaise, and lower limb sensory deficit. Significant investigations are given below. Which of the following drugs is associated with these findings?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given scenario points towards a diagnosis of Churg-Strauss syndrome. It is an eosinophilic vasculitis associated with the use of montelukast and zafirlukast. This is a very rarely reported side effect of these drugs.

These agents block the effects of the cysLTs (LTC4, LTD4, and LTE4) but they do not block the effect of LTB4, which is a chemoattractant for eosinophils and neutrophils. This can lead to eosinophilia.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 741
Online Resource, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22783603/

questions.stem: An asthmatic patient was brought to the ER in an agitated state. His respiratory rate was 32/min and pulse was 124/min. Pulse oximetry revealed a SpO2 of 88% on room air. Which of the following drugs is not useful in this scenario?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of acute severe asthma and cromolyn sodium is not useful in its treatment. It is indicated only for chronic prophylaxis.

Short-acting beta 2 agonists (SABA) and intravenous hydrocortisone are used in the treatment of acute severe asthma.

Ipratropium bromide can also be given in severe asthma exacerbations. It should be given after beta 2-agonists as they have a slower onset of bronchodilatory action. 





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 730
Tintinalli's Emergency Medicine , 8th Ed, page no. 215
Online Resource, https://ginasthma.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/GINA-Main-Report-2021-V2-WMS.pdf
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 20th Edition, Pg 1965

questions.stem: Omalizumab is added as a step-up therapy in a child with severe asthma, refractory to treatment. Which of the following is true about this drug?

options.label: C
options.text: Is indicated in acute severe asthma

options.label: D
options.text: Is a monoclonal antibody against IgE

questions.answerText: Is a monoclonal antibody against IgE
questions.solutionHtml:
Omalizumab is a monoclonal antibody against IgE.

It is used only in patients with very severe asthma (not acute severe asthma) who show poor symptom control even with step 4/5 measures as per GINA 2021 guidelines.

It can only be given to patients aged ≥6 years. It neutralizes circulating IgE and inhibits mast cell degranulation caused by IgE. It is administered subcutaneously.

Another drug used in severe asthma is mepolizumab. It is a monoclonal antibody acting against IL-5. 





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 14th Edition, Page no 890

questions.stem: A patient diagnosed with Churg-Strauss syndrome is started on Mepolizumab. This drug acts against:
questions.solutionHtml:
Mepolizumab is a monoclonal antibody against IL-5. It is indicated in: 

  • Selected (eosinophilic phenotype) patients with severe asthma
  • Churg-Strauss syndrome 
  • Hypereosinophilic syndrome 

IL-5 plays a pivotal role in eosinophilic inflammation and is also involved in eosinophil survival and priming.

Monoclonal antibodies against IL-5 approved for asthma are:

  • Mepolizumab
  • Reslizumab
  • Benralizumab




Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 742
Online Resource, https://reference.medscape.com/drug/nucala-mepolizumab-1000034#10
Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6292233/

questions.stem: What is the thromboxane receptor antagonist used in the treatment of asthma?
questions.solutionHtml:
Seratrodast is a thromboxane receptor antagonist indicated for use in long term prophylaxis of asthma. It is available and approved in India.

Option B- Rimonabant is a cannabinoid receptor antagonist that was investigated for weight gain but now withdrawn due to adverse psychological effects 

Option C- Sacubitril is a neprilysin inhibitor approved in fixed-dose combination with valsartan for heart failure patients.

Option D- Roflumilast is a phosphodiesterase 4 inhibitor which reduces eosinophil infiltration and inhibits inflammatory cell ,effective against smoke induced inflammation and emphysema.





Journal, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/10375998
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no: 740

questions.stem: In a case of acute exacerbation of asthma, salbutamol was given, however, no improvement was noticed. Intravenous corticosteroids and aminophylline were given and the condition improved. What is the probable mechanism by which the corticosteroids would have improved the condition?

options.label: A
options.text: Corticosteroids increase bronchial responsiveness to salbutamol

options.label: B
options.text: Corticosteroids cause direct bronchodilatation when used with xanthines

options.label: C
options.text: Corticosteroids indirectly increase the effect of xanthines on adenosine receptor

questions.answerText: Corticosteroids increase bronchial responsiveness to salbutamol
questions.solutionHtml:
Corticosteroids improved the condition by increasing the airway responsiveness to salbutamol.

Mechanism of action of corticosteroids in an acute asthma attack:

  • Increases responsiveness to β-2 agonists
  • Decreases mucous secretion
  • Decreases inflammatory cell response.

Steroids increase the transcription of β-2 receptor genes and hence increases responsiveness to β-2 agonists.

β-2 agonists increase the effect of steroids by enhancing the action of glucocorticoid receptors.

Theophylline increases the effects of steroids by activating the enzyme histone deacetylase which is the target for steroids as well.

Note: As per recent GINA 2021 guidelines, aminophyllines are no longer preferred in the management of acute severe asthma due to their low efficacy and poor safety profile.





Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, 7th edition, Page no 229
K.D Tripathi - Essentials of medical pharmacology 8th Edition, Page no 249

questions.stem: A patient has had 2 acute exacerbations of asthma over the span of 1-month despite being on therapy. Which of the following is a systemic steroid that can be used to treat her?
questions.solutionHtml:
Prednisolone is a systemic steroid used for maintenance therapy after an acute exacerbation of asthma.

Intravenous corticosteroids such as hydrocortisone are indicated if the lung function is predicted to be <30% or if there's poor response to nebulized β2 agonists. After the exacerbation, oral predisolone can be substituted with maximal beneficial effect at 30-40mg daily.

Inhaled corticosteroids commonly used in asthma are:

  • Beclomethasone dipropionate
  • Budesonide
  • Ciclesonide
  • Fluticasone
  • Mometasone




Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 14th Edition, Page: 888

questions.stem: An asthmatic patient presented to the ER with dyspnea and wheezing. Intake of which of the following is unlikely to have precipitated this?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of an acute exacerbation of asthma. Caffeine does not precipitate this.

Caffeine is a dietary xanthine similar in structure to methylxanthines (theophylline) which are used as adjuvants in the treatment of asthma. 

NSAIDs (like phenylbutazone, naproxen, and aspirin) inhibit the cyclooxygenase pathway thereby diverting arachidonic acid towards the lipoxygenase pathway. This increases the level of pro-inflammatory leukotrienes and can precipitate an acute asthma attack.





Tripathi's Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology 7th Edition, Page nos 221 and 229
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 741

questions.stem: A patient with mild episodic asthma is prescribed daily low-dose inhaled budesonide therapy. Which of the following conditions is he not at increased risk of developing?
questions.solutionHtml:
Inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) like budesonide do not increase the risk of developing carcinoma of the lung.

Common problems with the use of ICS: 

  • Hoarseness of voice
  • Weakness of voice (dysphonia)
  • Increased risk of bacterial and mycobacterial lung infection
  • Oropharyngeal candidiasis




Online Resource, https://www.uptodate.com/contents/major-side-effects-of-inhaled-glucocorticoids#H26407352

questions.stem: An elderly man with a 30-year history of smoking complains of breathing difficulty. A diagnosis of COPD is made, and treatment with a long-acting muscarinic antagonist is initiated. Which of the following will you not prescribe?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ipratropium is a short-acting muscarinic antagonist which is not used for the long-term management of COPD. It can be used to treat acute exacerbations.

The long-acting muscarinic antagonists (LAMAs) are:

  • Tiotropium
  • Glycopyrronium 
  • Umeclidinium
  • Aclidinium




Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page nos 735 and 736

questions.stem: Inhalational anticholinergics the mainstay of treatment in:
questions.solutionHtml:
Inhalational anticholinergics are the mainstay for the treatment of COPD.

Ipratropium is as effective as albuterol in patients with COPD. Longer-acting antimuscarinic agents, including tiotropium, aclidinium, and umeclidinium, are approved for maintenance therapy of COPD.

Anticholinergics are less effective than β-2 agonists as bronchodilators in asthma and are not the mainstay in the treatment of asthma.





Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology - 14th Edition, page no. 354

questions.stem: A chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) patient requires a step-up in therapy due to symptom persistence. Which PDE-4 inhibitor can you prescribe as an add-on drug to his treatment regimen?
questions.solutionHtml:
Roflumilast is a PDE-4 selective inhibitor approved for use in COPD. 

PDE-4 is the major isoform present in inflammatory cells and its inhibition results in higher anti-inflammatory effects. 

Option A: Seratrodast is a thromboxane receptor antagonist used in the prophylaxis of asthma. It decreases the bronchial hypersensitivity caused by thromboxane. 

Option C: Zileuton is a lipoxygenase inhibitor that can be used in the treatment of asthma.

Option D: Nedocromil is a mast cell stabilizer indicated in the prophylaxis of asthma. 





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 740

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs are antitussives?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dextromethorphan, morphine, and gabapentin are all antitussives.

Dextromethorphan is an NMDA receptor antagonist that suppresses the cough center.

Opiates like morphine have a central mechanism of action on the medullary cough center and are indicated for intractable cough associated with bronchial carcinoma. 

Gabapentin and pregabalin are GABA analogs that have been shown to benefit chronic idiopathic cough involving neural hypersensitivity.

Guaifenesin is an expectorant that is taken orally.

Carbocysteine is a mucolytic that reduces the disulfide bridges that bind glycoproteins to other proteins, such as albumin and secretory IgA. It is also taken orally and helps reduce the viscosity of sputum.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 14th Edition, Page no 893

questions.stem: A known case of CREST syndrome presents with dyspnea. On auscultation, a Graham-Steele murmur is heard. On further investigation, her pulmonary artery pressure is found to be 28 mm Hg. Which drug will you use to manage her condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
The clinical scenario points to a diagnosis of pulmonary artery hypertension (pulmonary artery pressure > 20mmHg) which can be managed using selective PDE-5 inhibitors.

Inhibition of PDE-5 in the pulmonary bed leads to a reduction in the hydrolysis of cGMP which causes pulmonary vasodilation.

Sildenafil and tadalafil are the PDE-5 inhibitors approved for use in PAH. 





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 577

questions.stem: Which of the following groups does riociguat belong to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Riociguat is a soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator (sGC), indicated in the treatment of pulmonary artery hypertension.

Riociguat increases the sensitivity of nitric oxide to sGC and also directly stimulates the sGC enzyme resulting in increased formation of cGMP. This leads to relaxation in the pulmonary vasculature.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 577, Figure 31-3

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs is a prostacyclin analog that can be added to the treatment regimen of a patient with pulmonary artery hypertension?
questions.solutionHtml:
Iloprost is a prostacyclin analog indicated in the management of pulmonary artery hypertension. It falls under the category of IP receptor (prostacyclin receptor) agonists.

Other drugs falling under the category of IP receptor agonists are:

  • Epoprostenol

  • Treprostinil

  • Iloprost

  • Selexipag

Option A: Sildenafil is a PDE-5 inhibitor. 

Option B: Misoprostol is a synthetic PGE1 analog. 

Option C: Dinoprost is a natural PGF2-alpha preparation. It should not be confused with dinoprostone which is a synthetic analogue of PGE2.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 14th Edition, Page no 701, 824

questions.stem: Which is a selective endothelin receptor A antagonist used in the management of pulmonary artery hypertension?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ambrisentan is a selective endothelin receptor A (ET-A) antagonist which is used in the management of pulmonary artery hypertension (PAH).

Bosentan, tezosentan, and macitantan are non-selective (ET-A and ET-B) endothelin receptor antagonists.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no. 484, 580

questions.stem: Dornase alfa is indicated in which of the following patients?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dornase alfa is indicated in patients with cystic fibrosis and as a rescue treatment for refractory atelectasis in newborn and pediatric populations.

Dornase alfa is a recombinant DNase 1 that digests neutrophil DNA deposited in the pulmonary mucus thereby reducing mucosal viscoelasticity.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 743
Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6712252/

questions.stem: Which of the following should not be prescribed with theophylline?
questions.solutionHtml:
Erythromycin should not be prescribed with theophylline.

Theophylline is mainly metabolized by CYP1A2 in the liver. Erythromycin inhibits CYP1A2 and thereby decreases the clearance of theophylline.

Factors decreasing the clearance of theophylline are:

  • Drugs - erythromycin, cimetidine, ciprofloxacin, allopurinol, fluvoxamine, zileuton, zafirlukast
  • Congestive heart failure
  • Liver disease
  • Pneumonia
  • Viral infection and vaccination
  • High-carbohydrate diet
  • Old age




Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no: 734

questions.stem: If codiene is coming to the market in combination with dextromethorphan as an anti-tussive, this combination _______

options.label: A
options.text: Should not be used due to risk of addiction

options.label: B
options.text: Can be used as both have different mechanism of action

options.label: C
options.text: Should not be used as it is irrational

options.label: D
options.text: Can be used to treat cough effectively

questions.answerText: Should not be used as it is irrational
questions.solutionHtml:
It is an irrational drug combination and should not be given.

Codeine is an opioid analgesic having specific antitussive action while dextromethorphan is a centrally active NMDA receptor antagonist that may be effective as an antitussive. Both are centrally acting antitussives, and do not provide any added advantage when combined. Hence it is an irrational drug combination.

Rational fixed-dose combination drugs for the treatment of cough usually contain:

  • A centrally acting anti-tussive (either codeine or dextromethorphan; not both), with
  • Antihistamines, decongestants and expectorants.

Option A - Both of these drugs carry a risk of addiction, but it is not the reason to not give the drug. The main reason is that the combination is irrational.

Options B & D - Both codeine and dextromethorphan have different mechanisms of action and can treat cough effectively. However, the combination of two centrally acting antitussives does not provide any added advantage compared to using one drug alone. Hence, the combination is irrational.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 377, 743
Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2432494/
